terms.summary: Paid-generation provenance is recorded for these effects and music. ElevenLabs general paid-output terms apply to effects; Music model-specific terms additionally exclude Studio Games on self-serve plans and prohibit licensing output as a music library. This unmonetized single-platform prototype is not commercial/Steam clearance. A commercial release must verify the actual distribution, applicable plan and all source rights. No open-content redistribution grant is made.

A sung song for the inn, from a composition plan: medieval tavern folk ballad; solo male baritone singer, warm and a little rough, English folk accent; lute fingerpicking; soft fiddle; slow 3/4 waltz around 84 BPM; D minor; intimate, sung in a small inn; acoustic period instruments. Lyrics (original, written for Tervain):
Verse 1: The thaw came down the mountain, / it broke the old stone gate, / the channels choked with silver silt, / and Rillford learned to wait.
Chorus: So ring, ring the drought bell, / ring it slow and low, / a bucket for the baker's house, / and one for the mill below.
Verse 2: The quarry wants its water, / the Sister wants her share, / the reeve counts every pail by hand, / and finds no answer there.
Verse 3: A stranger walked up from the strand / with no one's name to claim, / he climbed the hill and heard us ring, / and nothing stayed the same.
Final chorus: So ring, ring the drought bell, / ring it slow and low, / a bucket for the baker's house, / and one for the mill below.

A sung song for the inn, from a composition plan: lively medieval tavern drinking song; solo female folk singer, bright and cheeky, English folk accent; a few rough voices of drinkers joining on the chorus; fiddle, frame drum and lute; 6/8 jig around 112 BPM; D Dorian; played in a small crowded inn; acoustic period instruments. Lyrics (original, written for Tervain):
Verse 1: Hesper's oven's cold tonight, / the barrel's nearly dry, / but there's a crust upon the shelf / and a song to get us by.
Chorus: Oh, bread and water, water and bread, / a cup for the living, a cup for the dead, / and when the wheel goes round again / we'll drink to the mill instead!
Verse 2: Darin's cutting stone by day / and cursing it by night, / the steward counts his columns twice / and never gets them right.
Chorus: Oh, bread and water, water and bread, / a cup for the living, a cup for the dead, / and when the wheel goes round again / we'll drink to the mill instead!
Verse 3: So pass the jug along the bench, / and mind the floury floor, / the bell will ring a gladder note / than ever rang before.
Last chorus: Oh, bread and water, water and bread, / a cup for the living, a cup for the dead, / and when the wheel goes round again / we'll drink to the mill instead!
